t.3.26.1: But as Khara was setting out to face Rāma, the commander of the army, a rākṣasa named Triśiras, approached him and said this:
t.3.26.2: Appoint me, O valiant one, and turn back from this rash deed; behold Rāma, the mighty-armed, struck down in battle.
t.3.26.3: I promise you truly, and I touch my weapon as I swear it: I shall slay Rāma, who deserves death at the hands of all the rākṣasas.
t.3.26.4: Either I shall be his death in battle, or he shall be mine in this combat. Hold back your eagerness for battle and be a witness for a moment.
t.3.26.5: Either, when Rāma is slain, you will return joyful to Janasthāna, or, when I am slain, you will go forth to meet Rāma in battle.
t.3.26.6: Khara was won over by that Triśiras, who was drawn on by the lure of death; given leave with the words “Go, fight!”, he set out to face Rāghava.
t.3.26.8: Releasing masses of arrows in torrents like a great cloud pouring rain, he let forth a roar that was like the sound of a kettledrum soaked with water.
t.3.26.7: And Triśiras, on a shining chariot yoked with horses, rushed at Rāma in battle like a mountain with three peaks.
t.3.26.9: Seeing the rākṣasa Triśiras approaching, Rāghava met him with his bow, brandishing sharp arrows.
t.3.26.10: That great and tumultuous clash took place between Rāma and Triśiras, both exceedingly mighty, like the clash between a lion and an elephant.
t.3.26.11: Then Rāma, struck on the forehead by Triśiras with three arrows, angered and intolerant of the affront, spoke these furious words.
t.3.26.12: Ah, such is the strength of this rākṣasa, heroic in valor, by whose arrows I am struck on the forehead as if by flowers! Now receive my arrows too, loosed from the bowstring.
t.3.26.13: Having spoken thus, furious and enraged, he struck fourteen arrows like venomous serpents into the chest of Triśiras.
t.3.26.14: With four arrows with well-bent joints, the radiant one struck down his steeds, the four horses of his chariot.
t.3.26.15: With eight arrows he struck down the charioteer onto the floor of the chariot, and with a single arrow Rāma cut down his tall, upraised banner.
t.3.26.16: Then, as the night-roaming demon leapt up from that chariot whose horses and driver had been slain, Rāma pierced him in the heart with arrows, and he became stunned and motionless.
t.3.26.17: And he of immeasurable spirit, filled with indignation, struck down the three heads of that rākṣasa with three hundred swift arrows.
t.3.26.18: Sorely pierced by Rāma's arrows and spewing blood, that night-roamer fell to the ground, along with his own heads, which had fallen before him.
t.3.26.19: Then the surviving rākṣasas who had sought refuge with Khara, broken and routed, fled and did not stand their ground, like deer terrified by a tiger.
t.3.26.20: Seeing them fleeing, Khara, enraged, turned them back and himself rushed straight at Rāma, as Rāhu rushes at the moon.
